name: Hiboy KS4 Pro
notes: The scooter the simulator was first set up for. Specs from hiboy.com (45.3 x 18.9 x 48.2 in, 40.6 lb). Sale price read 2026-09-18 (list $950). Wh computed as V x Ah; battery location assumed deck.

name: Hiboy S2 Nova
notes: Price seen 2026-09-18 on hiboy.com (sale; list $659.99). Best Wh/$ in this slice (1.03 Wh/$). Specs from Hiboy spec table: 34.5 lb, unfolded 43.6 x 18.1 x 45.9 in, 36V 9Ah. Wh not published; 324 Wh = 36 V x 9 Ah computed. Tires are MIXED: 8.5 in solid front + 8.5 in pneumatic rear (tire_type field shows the front). Handlebar width taken from the unfolded W (18.1 in); Hiboy marketing copy separately says '19.2-inch extended handlebar' (0.488 m) - conflicting. Deck width and ground clearance not published. Battery location not stated by Hiboy; 'deck' inferred from S2-family design (no removable/stem pack), not confirmed by teardown. Front hub motor on S2 family.

name: Hiboy S2
notes: Price seen 2026-09-18 on hiboy.com (base variant without seat; seat/lock bundles $319.99-$349.99). Hiboy spec table: 35.49 lb, unfolded 45.7 x 17.0 x 47.2 in, 36V 7.5Ah, 17 mi. Geometry table: handlebar 16.9 in, deck 17.7 x 6.1 in, overall height 47.2 in, standing (deck-to-bar) height 41.3 in, folded height 19.3 in. Wh computed (36 x 7.5). Battery in deck confirmed by electricscooterinsider review ('battery is stored in the deck'); charge port is at top of stem. Third-party reviews list weight as 29.5-31.9 lb, conflicting with Hiboy's 35.49 lb; manufacturer figure used. Ground clearance not published.

name: Hiboy S3
notes: Price seen 2026-09-18 on hiboy.com. Spec table: 34.5 lb, unfolded 43.5 x 16.7 x 47.8 in, 36V 7.8Ah, 17 mi, 350 W rated / 460 W peak. Wh computed (36 x 7.8). The 'Geometry' block on the S3 page is a verbatim copy of the S2's (says 'S2 Scooter', height 47.2 in, deck 6.1 in wide) and contradicts the S3 spec table, so deck width left null; spec-table values used for L/W/H. Battery location not stated; 'deck' inferred from S2-family design, unconfirmed.

name: Hiboy S2 SE
notes: Price seen 2026-09-18 on hiboy.com (base variant; bundles up to $359.99). Spec table: 37.8 lb, unfolded 46.1 x 16.5 x 48.8 in, 36V 7.8Ah, 17 mi. Wh computed. Tires are MIXED: 10 in solid front + 10 in pneumatic rear (field shows front). Handlebar width taken from unfolded W (16.5 in). The page's 'Geometry' block is garbled (labels mismatched; a 6.3 in value is probably deck width = 0.160 m but unlabeled), so deck width left null. Battery location not stated; 'deck' inferred, unconfirmed.

name: Hiboy S2R Plus
notes: Price seen 2026-09-18 on hiboy.com (top edge of bracket; $419.99 with lock). Spec table: 31.5 lb, 44.1 x 16.9 x 49.2 in, 36V 8.7Ah, 22 mi, 350/500 W. Geometry: handlebar 16.9 in, deck 18.9 x 5.9 in, standing height 39.0 in, folded height 18.9 in. Wh computed (36 x 8.7 = 313 Wh). WEIGHT AMBIGUITY: Hiboy copy says '4.8lb removable battery' and 'just a 31.5lb frame' - unclear whether 31.5 lb includes the 2.18 kg battery; if not, total is ~16.5 kg. Removable key-locked battery lifts out of the DECK (confirmed by The Gadgeteer and electricscooterinsider S2R reviews and S2R manual), not the stem. Ground clearance not published.

name: NIU KQi 100P
notes: Price seen 2026-09-18 on shop.niu.com (list $429, in stock). Best-documented geometry in this slice: handlebar 52.0 cm wide / 122.9 cm high, body length 115.4 cm, deck 43.8 x 12.9 cm, deck top height 16.3 cm, clearance under deck 8.0 cm, folded height 50.5 cm. 38.1 lb incl. battery (17.3 kg per NIU Canada). NIU US lists only '48V, 243Wh'; 5.2 Ah comes from NIU Canada ('243WH / 48V5.2Ah'); 243/5.2 = 46.7 V so true nominal is ~46.8 V (13S), '48V' is the marketing class. Max load CONFLICT: NIU US says 265 lb (120 kg), NIU Canada says 100 kg (220 lb). Below the 270 Wh preference but 0.81 Wh/$. Tube-type pneumatic tires, front spring suspension (36 mm), rear hub motor, front drum brake. Battery location 'deck' per KQi-series underdeck pack design; not explicitly stated on the product page.

name: NIU KQi 100F
notes: Price seen 2026-09-18 on shop.niu.com (list $479). Same chassis/battery as KQi 100P but with folding handlebars: handlebar 58.7 cm wide (18.4 cm folded), 38.8 lb (17.6 kg). Other geometry identical to 100P per NIU page (height 122.9 cm, length 115.4 cm, deck 43.8 x 12.9 cm, clearance 8.0 cm). Ah (5.2) is taken from NIU Canada's 100P listing, which shares the 243 Wh pack - not separately published for the 100F. True nominal ~46.8 V. Max load 265 lb per NIU US (NIU Canada lists 100 kg for the 100P). Battery location 'deck' per KQi-series design, not explicitly stated.

name: Segway Ninebot E2 Plus II
notes: Price seen 2026-09-18 via store.segway.com catalog (final $349.99, regular $399.99, in stock); it was $320 in the Aug 2026 back-to-school sale. This is the ONLY Segway adult scooter in the $200-400 bracket today: E2 Pro (275 Wh) is $499.99 and E3 Pro (368 Wh) higher. Full spec table from Segway: 1081 x 447 x 1176 mm, 16.4 kg, nominal 21.6 V (6S, 25.2 V max charge), 10.2 Ah, 220 Wh, 300 W nominal / 500 W max, payload 90 kg (198 lb), max range 25 km (spec table; page title rounds to '16 miles'), 19 km at max speed. LOW-VOLTAGE 21.6 V system, unlike the 36 V norm. Tires are 8.1 in 'inner hollow shock-absorbing' (airless, hollow-core) - closest enum is solid/honeycomb. Handlebar width = overall W. Battery location 'deck': E2-family design has the pack under the footboard with the charge port on the footboard (from a search-result summary of the E2 Plus manual; manual page itself could not be fetched, so treat as likely but not directly verified). Deck width/clearance not published. Below the 270 Wh preference (0.63 Wh/$).

name: Gotrax G3 Plus
notes: Price seen 2026-09-18 on gotrax.com ($319, list $499) but marked SOLD OUT there; riderguide quotes $399 street. Gotrax publishes NO dimensions for this model (no L/W/H, handlebar, deck or clearance) and no peak motor power -> nulls. Spec table: 300 W front hub motor, 36V 6.0Ah (216 Wh), 34.5 lb, 220 lb limit, 10 in pneumatic, 18 mi claimed (riderguide tested 9.8 mi, 35.0 lb). Battery location 'deck' inferred from Gotrax's replacement-battery listing (detachable packs ship attached to the scooter underside); not confirmed for G3 Plus specifically. Gotrax's only larger-battery commuter near the bracket, the G4 (36V 10.4Ah = 374 Wh, 37 lb), is $449 and sold out on gotrax.com, so it was excluded. Other in-bracket Gotrax models are smaller: XR Pro 36V 5.2Ah $349.99, Fusion 36V 5.8Ah $349. Weak Wh/$ (0.68).

name: Xiaomi Electric Scooter 4 Lite (2nd Gen)
notes: LOW CONFIDENCE ENTRY. Xiaomi has no US store for scooters; US availability is via Amazon/third-party importers. The $396 price is a tracker figure from scooterrank.com (Amazon-tracked, 'last 30 days'), NOT a live retailer price I could load (Amazon/Walmart block fetching). From mi.com global spec page (authoritative): 16.2 kg, 221 Wh, 25 km range, 300 W rated / 500 W max, 10 in pneumatic, 100 kg load, charger max output 25.2 V. Nominal voltage is NOT published; 21.6 V is inferred from the 25.2 V (6S) charger. Ah not published by Xiaomi (scooterrank says 9.6 Ah/242 Wh, a reseller says 10.4 Ah/225 Wh - both conflict with mi.com's 221 Wh) -> null. Dimensions on mi.com are image-only; 1141 x 440 x 1224 mm is from a reseller listing (classic-phones.com), corroborated only for height by scooterrank (1.22 m). Handlebar width = overall W. Battery location not verified (1st-gen 4 Lite and this model differ in layout) -> unknown. No other Xiaomi model is in the bracket (4 Lite 1st gen ~$506, Scooter Pro ~$484, 4 Pro $599+).

name: Hover-1 Renegade
notes: HIGH-VOLTAGE PICK (above 48 V class). Wh/$ = 2.09, best in slice. AVAILABILITY CAVEAT: $299.99 is the price on the official page (list $699.99) but it showed 'Out of stock' on 2026-09-18; Wellbots lists $399.00, also sold out; Amazon/Walmart/Tractor Supply listings exist but could not be fetched (bot walls). Battery '54V, 11.6Ah (60 Cell)' is from the official manual spec table; 60 cells is consistent with 15S4P of 2.9 Ah cells (15 x 3.6 V = 54 V nominal), so 54 V appears to be a true nominal, not a charge voltage. Wh is computed (54 x 11.6), not published. Motor: dual 450 W hub motors (front + rear), 900 W total is what is published; rated vs peak not distinguished. Height/length/width converted from manual 'Open Size 47.5 x 20.5 x 44.7 in'; handlebar_width is the overall-width figure. Claimed range 33 mi (manual also says 55 km; support FAQ says 31 mi). Battery location 'deck' is inferred from the manual parts diagram, where the charging port callout sits at the front of the foot deck below the folding hinge; not explicitly stated. Deck width and ground clearance not published.

name: Evercross EV10K Pro
notes: CONFLICTING BATTERY SPEC on the manufacturer's own site: the product-page spec table says '36V,12Ah' (432 Wh computed, Wh/$ 1.44) but the collection listing for the same product says 36V 10.4Ah (374 Wh, Wh/$ 1.25). Treat 10.4 Ah as the safer assumption; Wh is never published. Showed 'Sold out' on the official US store on 2026-09-18 at $299.99 (list $599.99); it is sold on Amazon/Walmart but those pages could not be fetched. Motor: '500W' is described as peak power (Walmart title: '500W Peak Power Motor'); rated power not published. Tires: title says 10" honeycomb, spec table says 10" solid. 150 kg / 330 lb max load is unusually high for a 16 kg scooter - treat as marketing. Range published as 35-40 km (22-25 mi). handlebar_width is the overall-width figure (110 x 51 x 118 cm). Battery location not stated (likely deck, unverified).

name: iScooter i10
notes: Largest in-stock pack in the bracket (Wh/$ 1.42). Official page publishes '42V 15Ah' - 42 V is the full-charge voltage of a 10S pack; GeekBuying and iGeekPhone list it as 36V 15Ah / 540 Wh, which is what is recorded. 540 Wh at $380 from a white-label brand is plausible only with cheap cells; real capacity unverified by any independent test. One third-party page (punkride, likely a different EU variant) claims 48V 15Ah and 24-25 kg - treated as unreliable. '650W' motor is not labelled rated or peak on the official page (almost certainly peak; rated likely ~350-400 W, unpublished). Dimensions from official '115 x 48.5 x 120 cm'; handlebar_width is the overall-width figure. Rear hub motor, front+rear suspension. Battery location not published (thick-deck design, likely deck, unverified).

name: Hover-1 Stealth
notes: Wh/$ 1.36. AVAILABILITY CAVEAT: official page shows $345.00 (list $899.99) but 'Out of stock' on 2026-09-18; Woot deal at $299.99 also sold out; Amazon listing B0CZF8T632 exists but could not be fetched. Wh computed (36 x 13), not published. Battery is advertised as removable, but neither the product page nor Woot says whether it sits in the stem or the deck - left as unknown; this matters a lot for CoM, check photos before using. Tires are 10" tubeless pneumatic. '500W brushless' not labelled rated/peak. Unfolded 43.7 x 18 x 50.7 in - the 50.7 in (1.288 m) height is unusually tall for this class; it is what Hover-1 publishes. handlebar_width is the overall-width figure. Max load 220 lb. Charge time 10 h.

name: KuKirin S1 Max
notes: Wh/$ 1.34. Price $279.99 (list $359.99) on KuKirin's global official store with a US-warehouse shipping option; stock indicator on the page was contradictory ('Many in stock' and 'Only 0 left'). Wh computed (36 x 10.4), not published. Unfolded size 108.2 x 50 x 110 cm is from reseller Halo Knights (official page only gave folded 1082 x 500 x 460 mm); weight given there as 16 +/- 0.5 kg. handlebar_width is the overall-width figure. Speed-limited to 25 km/h (EU-spec design). Small 8" solid honeycomb tires. Battery location not stated (KuKirin S-series are deck-battery designs, but unverified for this model).

name: AOVOPRO ES80
notes: Wh/$ 1.26 at $299. PRICE AMBIGUITY: the official store has two ES80 listings - the US-warehouse listing at $299.00 (used here) and a '10.5Ah long range' listing at $179.00 (below the $200 floor; Wh/$ would be 2.11). Same scooter; the store also warns units may arrive rebadged as LP80/AV01/TX01. SKEPTICISM: 36V 10.5Ah (378 Wh, Wh figure from punkride, equals V x Ah) in a 12 kg Xiaomi-M365-clone chassis is doubtful - the genuine M365 is 12.5 kg with 7.8 Ah, and the claimed range is only 30 km, which fits ~7.8 Ah better than 10.5 Ah. Treat real capacity as possibly ~280 Wh. Battery location 'deck' because it is an M365-pattern clone (under-deck pack, front hub motor), not from a manufacturer statement. Tires: official says 'anti-skid solid', punkride says honeycomb solid. handlebar_width is the overall-width figure (1070 x 430 x 1100 mm).

name: iScooter i9M
notes: Wh/$ 1.13 on the published figure, 0.96 on the honest one. INFLATED Wh: page publishes '42V 7.5Ah, 315Wh' - 315 = 42 x 7.5 uses the full-charge voltage; nominal is 36 V x 7.5 Ah = 270 Wh. Published 315 is recorded per instructions; use 270 Wh in the sim. Range published as '18 miles (25km)' which is self-inconsistent (18 mi = 29 km; 29 recorded). Official page has folded/unfolded labels swapped ('Unfolded 44 x 17 x 18.9 in, Folded 44 x 17 x 45.7 in'); 45.7 in taken as unfolded height. '500W' motor is not labelled rated/peak and is likely peak (this chassis class normally carries a 350 W rated motor). Battery location 'deck' inferred from M365-pattern layout, not stated. handlebar_width is the overall-width figure.

name: Hover-1 Helios
notes: Wh/$ 1.03. Best-documented model in this slice (official manual spec table). Price: $349.00 in stock at Wellbots (2026-09-18); official store shows $299.99 but 'Out of stock'. Weight: manual says '40.3 lbs (19kg)' - these disagree (40.3 lb = 18.28 kg, 19 kg = 41.9 lb); lb-derived value recorded. Max load '240 lbs (110kg)' likewise (240 lb = 108.9 kg); Wellbots says 264 lb. Wh computed (36 x 10), not published; Wellbots lists '42V/10Ah' (charge voltage). Motor '500W brushless' in the manual, but the Amazon title calls it '500 Watts Max Power', so 500 W may be peak. Dimensions from manual 'Open Size 113 x 51.5 x 119 cm'; handlebar_width is the overall-width figure. Battery is removable and key-locked (manual ships '2 battery keys') yet the same manual also says 'the battery is built-in and should not be removed' (boilerplate). Stem vs deck is NOT stated anywhere I could read - left unknown; check photos.

name: isinwheel S9 Pro
notes: Wh/$ 1.00. Below the 300 Wh preference; included as the cheapest sane M365-pattern baseline, in stock at $279.99 (list $399.99). Weight published as '27.5 lbs (13.5 kg)' - these disagree (27.5 lb = 12.47 kg); lb-derived value recorded, which matches the ~12.5 kg M365 chassis. Capacity: product page says 7.8 Ah, collection listing says 7.5 Ah. Wh computed (36 x 7.8), not published. Only two dimensions published (1060 x 1090 mm, L x H); width/handlebar width not given. Two listings exist for the S9 Pro: one specced with 8.5" pneumatic tires (used here) and one described as solid honeycomb. Battery location 'deck' inferred from M365-pattern layout, not stated. 19-mile range claim from 281 Wh is optimistic (~9 Wh/km).
